Definition: and other moods and persons of the same tense; from G1909 and G1492; to regard (favorably or otherwise):--behold, look upon.
BiblicalUsage: Epeidon is the aorist form of looking upon with favour — God regarding His people. Elizabeth says the Lord looked on her to take away her reproach, and the church prays, Lord, behold their threatenings, and grant boldness to speak.
TheologicalSignificance: The comfort of this word is that God sees, I believe: He looked on Elizabeth, and He looks on His threatened people still.
